note.question: How should a food-delivery platform and restaurants divide food revenue, delivery revenue, and delivery cost so that commission competition does not feature distant restaurants or restrict delivery inefficiently?
note.overview: Multiple restaurants first choose commission bids for delivery discounts and scarce featured slots; the platform then chooses restaurant-specific delivery fees and featured listings, and the paper derives the subgame-perfect equilibrium and a coordinating contract.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In stage 1, restaurants simultaneously choose commission rates at or above the platform's base rate. In stage 2, after observing commissions, the platform chooses a low, high, or no-delivery outcome for each restaurant and chooses at most K restaurants to feature. Demand and profits are realized. Restaurants pay commissions both to induce lower delivery fees and to compete for featured display.
